observations.claim: Calibration set has 36 samples and only 12 wavelengths; profile flagged high-frequency noise (0.499) and scattered variation (0.243) with low SNR; target std ~1.71 a.u.
No spikes present (spike_row_fraction=0), so despiking is not indicated; baseline drift is modest (0.115).
Method cards note PLS suits collinear NIR with quantitative targets and SG smoothing targets high-frequency noise while preserving broad bands; cards are evidence, not an execution order.

proposal.rationale: Both alternatives attack the two strongest descriptive flags (noise vs scatter) with different model families. I select A (PLS + SG smoothing) as the first experiment: PLS is the standard collinear-NIR regression baseline, SG smoothing with a small window (7) directly targets the highest score (high-frequency noise 0.499) while limiting peak distortion on a coarse 12-point axis, and n_components=4 is a conservative latent count relative to 36 samples. B remains a distinct scatter-focused comparison to revisit if A shows residual scatter structure. Test stays sealed.
uncertainties: Whether high-frequency noise or scatter variation dominates the residual is not established from the descriptive profile.
Optimal SG window/order and PLS latent count are unknown at this sample size.

expected_improvement.text_expectation: If the SG-smoothed PLS model fits, Cal CV RMSE is expected to be moderate-to-low given target std ~1.71; a high or overfit CV RMSE would indicate that smoothing alone is insufficient and a scatter-focused change is warranted.

quality.recommendation: 模型质量达标，可继续后续流程；建议关注 bias 与过拟合风险。
